title: Axial-flux motor
summary: Implemented the transmitter, receiver and Arduino code for the shared motor build, documented in bench footage.
work: Designed, wound and assembled an axial-flux motor; the photographs show nine coils and a common-axis rotor assembly.
A potentiometer and ESP32 on the handheld copper-board controller send the speed command wirelessly to a motor-side ESP32, which controls the ESC between the supply and motor.
limits: The ESP32/ESC topology follows the project owner's description. The generic supply, firmware timing and drive percentage are illustrative; no measured speed, rating or efficiency is inferred.

title: Three-axis camera gimbal
summary: Developed most of the Arduino code and shared the build and gyroscope cross-checks; CAD adaptation by Tuna.
work: Three nested servo axes support a payload; the mechanical design was adapted from an internet design.
The project used a phone gyro workaround after an MPU sensor problem. The compared datasets were not synchronized.
The exhibit demonstrates ideal counter-rotation, rather than reproducing the original firmware or measured control performance.
limits: No validated PID accuracy or unlimited physical servo travel. The full-turn sliders are exhibit orientations.
credit: Student mechatronics project; adapted mechanical design, original creator not identified in available evidence.

title: Battery management system
summary: Completed most development and all Simulink simulations for the four-cell BMS; PCB drawings by Atahan.
work: EE401 planned the system; EE402 documented the outcomes, instrumentation and prototype.
The balancing model moves charge using a switched capacitor. This simulation is distinct from the photographed physical hardware.
Visitors change individual cells, load and temperature to explore balancing and thermal load cutoff.
limits: Long-term hardware balancing and protection validation was unfinished. Displayed values and accelerated time are illustrative.
credit: Senior-year team project; shared hardware and simulation evidence.

title: Boundary-scanning Zumo robot
summary: Developed most of the robot project, combining boundary navigation with IR detection counts and LED/buzzer reporting.
work: Calibrate reflectance sensors, move toward the white edge while avoiding IR detections, then scan and return.
Store counts from ten trials and signal the maximum through the LED and buzzer.
Five illustrated arrangements succeeded; one arrangement at the boundary failed.
limits: No SLAM, object-identity map or statistical accuracy claim. Repeated IR detections can count the same object. This geometric exhibit simplifies traction, timing and sensor optics.
credit: Yunus Emre Ozan and Seyit Kubilay Uluçay. Uses Pololu Zumo libraries.

title: Power flow & economic dispatch
summary: A MATLAB App Designer interface for an educational network and generator cost model.
work: Two modes expose power flow and economic dispatch with three generators.
The dispatch callback solves equal marginal-cost equations with a demand constraint, then calculates quadratic costs.
The source includes fixed network coefficients and UI controls for generator settings.
limits: Static source review only; the MATLAB runtime and solver were not validated here. Not an operational grid planning tool; feasibility limits need separate checking.
credit: Named individual MATLAB submission by Kubilay Uluçay.

title: Off-grid residential PV design
summary: A PVsyst sizing and feasibility study for a house in Kocaeli.
work: The source report proposes eight 580 W modules (4.64 kW) and approximately 38.3 kWh stored energy.
Weather, load, storage and winter availability drive the simulation trade-offs.
The financial analysis uses May 2025 assumptions and finds poor simple payback, around 62 years.
limits: Simulated proposal, not an installed system. Historical component prices and payback are not current recommendations.
credit: Seyit Kubilay Uluçay and Mehmet Fatih Karaosman.

title: Wind-farm interconnection trade-offs
summary: Compared 27 configurations and recommended Experiment 9: CONDOR connections to PETE and PAI.
work: PowerWorld cases compare cost, loss and overload constraints for a hypothetical 200 MW wind-farm connection.
The analysis narrows feasible configurations instead of assuming the lowest-loss case is automatically best.
limits: A classroom network study, not a built wind farm or a commercial engineering recommendation.

title: PLC sequences: traffic lights & toy claw
summary: Developed sequence logic and checked simulated traffic-light modes and claw-game control.
work: Traffic-light logic models normal and after-hours modes with HMI controls.
The claw game uses a coin input, a 90-second positioning window and a staged gripper sequence.
The shared team report documents both scenarios and the issues encountered during testing.
limits: Academic simulation; no roadside deployment or physical claw-machine build is confirmed. Peer-only Lab3 and provided solution files are excluded.
credit: Berke Çeçen, Efe Can Özhan, Genco Güven and Kubilay Uluçay.

title: Bench measurements & diode curves
summary: Selected bench records show multimeter readings, resistor-current calculations and diode I–V observations.
work: Built the lab circuits and recorded node and resistor voltage measurements.
Compared the recorded current–voltage behavior of different diode types.
limits: Selected original bench pages, not a complete lab series or new measurements.
credit: Original EE301 bench records by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, Fall 2023.

title: Sensors, timing & motor response
summary: Four selected studies connect analog sensing, timing waveforms, two-board I2C and proportional motor response.
work: Recorded analog-input and reflectance-sensor behavior and an oscillator timing capture.
Adapted course examples for a button-to-LED I2C link between two Arduino boards.
Documented motor-position observations at different proportional gains; the later full-PID extension was not verified.
limits: Selected original source pages with original page references, not a complete lab series or a validated full-PID controller.
credit: Original ME417 records by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, March–May 2024; course examples retain their authorship.

title: Floor sensing in an R&D team
summary: R&D internship contributions spanning sensing tests, data acquisition, Minitab analysis and embedded integration.
work: Supported test setup, sensing/data acquisition and preprocessing for robot-vacuum floor-detection work.
Contributed to Minitab analysis/modeling, embedded integration, testing, iteration and documentation within the R&D team.
limits: Internal reports, images, code, identifiers, model parameters and proprietary results are excluded. This is a team internship contribution, not a claim of sole ownership, inventorship or production deployment.
credit: R&D internship contribution by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay within Beko Advanced Sensor Technologies, July–August 2024.
